chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the child who steals, he said: He is excused once. If he repeats, his fingertips are cut, or they are scratched until they bleed. If he repeats, his fingers are cut. If he repeats, he is cut lower than that.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a child who commits theft?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the graduated penal code for a child (sabi) who has reached the age of discernment but is not yet fully liable for hadd punishments. The punishment escalates from exemption to cutting fingertips, then fingers, and finally lower limbs with each subsequent offense. This progression reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of 'ta'zir' (discretionary punishment) tailored to a child's capacity, emphasizing correction over retribution.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the child who steals. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be excused from it once. So if he repeats, his fingertips would be cut, or they would be scratched until they bleed. So he if repeats, his fingers would be cut. So if he repeats, he would be cut lower than that’.
